patch_description: Replace the exponentially-weighted moving average (which introduces lag and still allows noise-driven slope reversals) with a zero-phase local polynomial (Savitzky-Golay style) filter. A degree-2 polynomial fit over each sliding window passes through the data with no phase delay, preserves linear and quadratic trends (greatly reducing lag error and slope changes), and its least-squares nature suppresses noise more effectively than a weighted mean, reducing false reversals. Centering the fit on the window means no directional bias toward past samples, so responsiveness is maintained. This addresses all four objectives: slope-change minimization, lag minimization, tracking accuracy, and false-reversal avoidance, while keeping O(W) work per sample (efficient). We also make the basic filter use the same approach so both code paths benefit.
